title: Choose Azure CNI Overlay or Pod Subnet deliberately
description: Prefer Azure CNI Overlay for efficient address use, or Azure CNI Pod Subnet when directly routable pod addresses are required. Validate OS and policy-engine compatibility. Kubenet is a legacy model retiring on 31 March 2028; do not select it for new deployments.

documentation.title: Choose Azure CNI Overlay or Pod Subnet deliberately

title: Plan node and pod address capacity including upgrade surge
description: Size address space for the actual network model, maximum nodes, maxPods, scale-out, and concurrent surge upgrades. Overlay separates pod and node address space; flat networking consumes VNet pod addresses. Include private endpoints, load balancers, peering, and future growth.

documentation.title: Plan node and pod address capacity including upgrade surge

title: Choose supported L7 ingress and plan Gateway API migration
description: Use a supported ingress or Gateway API implementation for HTTP routing, TLS, and policy. Upstream Ingress NGINX maintenance ended in March 2026; AKS application routing NGINX critical-security-patch support runs through November 2026. Evaluate application routing Gateway API, Application Gateway for Containers, or Istio ingress against feature and support requirements.

documentation.title: Choose supported L7 ingress and plan Gateway API migration

title: Protect internet-facing HTTP applications with an appropriate WAF
description: Choose a supported WAF architecture, such as Azure Front Door Premium or Application Gateway WAF, when required by the threat model. Tune managed rules, restrict origin access, validate TLS and health probes, and test that the origin cannot bypass the WAF.

documentation.title: Protect internet-facing HTTP applications with an appropriate WAF

title: Restrict ingress hostnames and Gateway API delegation
description: Constrain approved hostnames, cross-namespace references, and who can attach routes to shared gateways. Use admission controls and Gateway API allowedRoutes/ReferenceGrant rules as appropriate; test that tenants cannot claim another application hostname.

documentation.title: Restrict ingress hostnames and Gateway API delegation

title: Expose only the load balancers that need public access
description: Use internal load balancers for private services and public endpoints only for intentional internet-facing applications. An internal load balancer still needs authentication, network controls, DNS, and a tested access path.

documentation.title: Expose only the load balancers that need public access

title: Enforce pod network policy using a supported engine
description: Apply and test ingress and egress policies with explicit DNS and dependency allowances. Azure CNI Powered by Cilium is recommended for supported Linux configurations; validate Windows support separately. A configured policy engine without effective policies does not isolate workloads.

documentation.title: Enforce pod network policy using a supported engine

title: Configure default network policies in each namespace
description: Start by creating a deny all policy in each namespace and then add specific policies.

documentation.title: Recipes of best default network policies
Calico global network policy

title: Filter egress traffic with AzFW/NVA if your security requirements mandate it (egress lockdown)
description: Use Azure Firewall to secure and control all egress traffic going outside of the cluster.

documentation.title: Egress traffic requirements

title: Don't expose your container registry on Internet
description: When possible, use private link to only allow private network to reach your registry.

documentation.title: Azure Container Registry Private Link

title: Test workload access to metadata and host-network services
description: Explicitly test access to 169.254.169.254 and host-network workloads from ordinary application pods. Network policy behavior depends on the data plane and host-network semantics. AKS IMDS restriction is documented as preview and does not restrict host-network pods; assess support terms before adoption and minimize node identity permissions.

documentation.title: Test workload access to metadata and host-network services

title: Use private clusters if your requirements mandate it
description: In a private cluster, the control plane or API server has internal IP addresses and is not exposed to Internet
detail: Plan private DNS and an approved network path for administrators and deployment runners, such as a connected management host, VPN, or ExpressRoute. Azure Bastion provides access to a management VM rather than acting as a direct Kubernetes API proxy. Review command invoke permissions separately because that management-plane path can reach a private cluster without direct client network connectivity.

documentation.title: Create a private cluster (using private link)
API Server VNet Integration
Use azure CLI to run command on a private cluster
Use public DNS with a private cluster

title: Choose global routing based on protocol and failover requirements
description: Use Azure Front Door for global HTTP(S) edge routing and WAF integration, or Traffic Manager for DNS-based routing of supported endpoints. Configure health checks, TLS, DNS TTLs, origin restrictions, and failover tests; neither service automatically replicates application state.

documentation.title: Choose global routing based on protocol and failover requirements

title: Set maxPods explicitly for the chosen networking model
description: Check the default and supported maximum pod density for the actual OS, network model, VM size, and provisioning method. Do not assume a universal default of 30. Account for DaemonSets, system reservations, IP capacity, and storage attachment limits.

documentation.title: Set maxPods explicitly for the chosen networking model

title: If using a public API endpoint, restrict the IP addresses that can access it
description: To improve the security of your clusters and minimize the risk of attacks, we recommend limiting the IP address ranges that can access the API server.

documentation.title: Secure access to the API server using authorized IP address ranges

title: Choose and monitor an explicit outbound connectivity design
description: Choose a supported outboundType such as NAT gateway, load balancer, or user-defined routing based on throughput and inspection requirements. Size SNAT capacity and allow AKS dependencies. NAT Gateway is not a firewall; private clusters still need an explicit egress plan.

documentation.title: Choose and monitor an explicit outbound connectivity design

title: Evaluate Pod Subnet allocation when flat pod routing is needed
description: For VNet-routable pod IPs, evaluate Azure CNI Pod Subnet dynamic or static block allocation against supported features and scale limits. Plan separate node and pod subnet capacity; use Overlay when direct pod reachability is not required.

documentation.title: Evaluate Pod Subnet allocation when flat pod routing is needed

title: Use private endpoints or service endpoints where appropriate
description: For PaaS dependencies, select private endpoints or supported service endpoints based on service capability and trust boundaries. Configure private DNS and public-access restrictions explicitly; a private AKS API endpoint does not make workload dependencies private.

documentation.title: Use private endpoints or service endpoints where appropriate

title: Adopt a service mesh only for explicit application requirements
description: Evaluate a supported mesh, such as the AKS Istio add-on, when service identity, mutual TLS, traffic policy, or detailed telemetry justify its operational cost. Validate supported revisions, upgrades, resource overhead, and failure behavior; a mesh is not a prerequisite for every microservice application.

documentation.title: About service meshes

title: Use a bring-your-own CNI only with clear support ownership
description: Use bring-your-own CNI only when its capabilities are necessary and the team can operate and support it. Review AKS support boundaries, Kubernetes and OS compatibility, IPAM, policy enforcement, upgrades, and recovery; Azure does not operate a third-party CNI on your behalf.

documentation.title: Bring your own Container Network Interface (CNI) plugin for AKS

title: Use per-node-pool subnets when the network design requires them
description: Evaluate separate node-pool subnets for address-space organization, routing, or security requirements. Validate support for the selected Azure CNI mode and subnet delegation, private DNS, and policy behavior; subnet separation alone is not tenant isolation.

documentation.title: Add a node pool with a unique subnet

title: Reserve nonoverlapping service, pod, node, and connected-network ranges
description: Validate service, pod, node-subnet, peered-VNet, VPN, and on-premises address ranges before deployment. Apply the rules of the selected network model, including Overlay routing and masquerading behavior, and test reachability to all dependencies. Address conflicts can make destinations unreachable.

documentation.title: Pod CIDR, Service CIDR and Subnet CIDR
Use the right CIDR ranges for networking parameters

title: Validate DNS resolution and private-zone ownership
description: Test cluster DNS, upstream DNS, private endpoints, and cross-network name resolution from pods and deployment runners. Monitor DNS latency and failures, scale CoreDNS when needed, and evaluate LocalDNS only against current feature availability and workload requirements.

documentation.title: Validate DNS resolution and private-zone ownership

title: Evaluate Azure CNI Powered by Cilium for Linux data planes
description: Use the supported managed Cilium data plane for compatible Linux workloads. Validate NetworkPolicy behavior and migration constraints; advanced L7, FQDN, and observability features can require Advanced Container Networking Services and additional cost.

documentation.title: Evaluate Azure CNI Powered by Cilium for Linux data planes

title: Manage TLS certificate issuance and renewal
description: Inventory external and internal certificates, automate issuance and renewal through a supported integration, and alert before expiry. Validate trust chains, TLS policy, secret rotation, and application reload behavior without relying on manual certificate replacement.

documentation.title: Manage TLS certificate issuance and renewal
